Send numeric data to the browser in single precision

Source: R/widget.R
as_float32.Rd

Marks a numeric vector or matrix to be sent to plotly.js as a float32 typed array: 4 bytes per value instead of 8, halving the size of the widget's data and of plotly.js's copy of it. Use it in trace properties, or on data frame columns used in formula properties (x = ~col). Set options(plotly.core.float32 = TRUE) to send all numeric arrays in single precision.

Usage

as_float32(x)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector or matrix.

Value

x, marked with class plotly_float32.

Details

Single precision keeps about 7 significant digits: values shown in hover labels and returned by event_data() change (0.1 becomes 0.100000001490116), whole numbers above 2^24 (16,777,216) aren't exact and numeric times in seconds since 1970 are only accurate to minutes. Vectors of whole numbers (in the 32-bit integer range) are always sent as integers without loss, and date-times as text, so neither is affected. WebGL traces (e.g. go_scattergl()) draw in single precision anyway.

Examples

n <- 1e4
data.frame(x = rnorm(n), y = rnorm(n)) |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattergl(x = ~as_float32(x), y = ~as_float32(y), mode = "markers")
